verdict.rationale: Brex documents an official MCP server that lets AI assistants manage expenses and review transactions. It also documents a Transactions API that lists settled card transactions, an Accounting API for managing accounting data, and a Fields API for single-select coding dropdowns, so an external agent can plausibly read spend and write some coding back. However, the evidence never shows a filter for uncoded transactions, an endpoint for writing categories or policy flags onto expenses for review, or policy-violation data beyond travel bookings. Brex's own AI agents that categorize spend and flag violations are first-party features, not an agent-accessible API. Missing for 10: documented uncoded-transaction query, explicit write-back of coding/categories to expenses via API/MCP, API-exposed expense policy flags, review-queue submission, hands-on corroboration.
